description: the Head Start public age bridge is wrong for ordinary and dual program contexts; paragraph-(c)/participation outputs omit the statutory subject predicate; numeric runtime leaves fail OPEN with no domain contract

triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The single public age bridge (participant_meets_age_requirements_under_paragraph_b) was gated on `tribal_program or migrant_or_seasonal_program`, so it denied paragraph-(b) age satisfaction to ordinary Head Start participants and let one program's age test (e.g. the (b)(1)/(b)(2) branch) satisfy the other program's requirement in dual contexts, while the paragraph-(c) and participation outputs dropped the §1302.12(c)(1) subject predicate ("A pregnant woman or a child is eligible if") and so fired for persons who are neither a child nor a pregnant woman.
triage.triage_notes: Read the pinned provision (us/regulation/45/1302/12, corpus release us-rulespec-2026-07-24-snap-cms-pit-union): (b) states age rules for Early Head Start, Head Start Preschool, and Migrant or Seasonal separately with no Tribal/Migrant gating on the ordinary case; (c)(1) reads "A pregnant woman or a child is eligible if"; (e) requires a Tribal program + approved service area + paragraph (b); (f) requires at least one family member with income primarily from agricultural employment + paragraph (b). Multi-defect repair in one module: (1) scope/contamination in the shared age bridge — pre-fix the local rule participant_meets_age_requirements_under_paragraph_b also fed the imported us:regulations/45-cfr/1302/12#tribal_service_area_participant_eligible and #migrant_or_seasonal_participant_eligible, whose own formulas consume that same open name, so one bridge served both program scopes; the fix drops those two imports and composes (e)/(f) locally from three newly declared inputs (head_start_tribal_program, head_start_participant_in_approved_tribal_service_area, head_start_family_has_primary_agricultural_employment_income). (2) missing statutory subject predicate added to head_start_paragraph_c_path_satisfied, head_start_additional_allowance_path_satisfied, and head_start_participation_path_satisfied. (3) a secondary polarity_or_logic defect — fail-open numeric runtime leaves replaced by the fail-closed head_start_runtime_inputs_valid contract, now ANDed into every rule; if a reviewer prefers one kind per finding, this module supports both wrong_entity_or_scope (primary, 2 of 3 named findings) and polarity_or_logic (secondary). The quote is verbatim from MaxGhenis's blind-review comment on PR #1010, which the bundle stores under issue_comments rather than reviews (reviews/review_comments are empty); it is a review in substance. The commit body is empty, so all stated reasoning comes from that review. No effective dates, thresholds, or multipliers changed (all versions stay effective_from 2021-01-01); the 100%/130% logic is untouched. Note the public rule rename participant_meets_age_requirements_under_paragraph_b -> head_start_ordinary_or_tribal_age_requirement_met, an interface-breaking rename bundled with the fidelity fix. Companion test file us/policies/hhs/head_start/eligibility_pipeline.test.yaml grew by 306 lines in the same commit. The review's top finding (WIC 185% federal maximum vs the operative State agency guideline) concerns a different module and is not in this commit.
triage.verifier_justification: My refutation attempt fails on the core claim: the pre-fix module published a single `participant_meets_age_requirements_under_paragraph_b` gated on `tribal_program ... or migrant_or_seasonal_program ...`, and the imported regulation rules `tribal_service_area_participant_eligible` (`tribal_program and participant_in_approved_service_area and participant_meets_age_requirements_under_paragraph_b`) and `migrant_or_seasonal_participant_eligible` both bound that one contaminated predicate by name, so in a dual context one program's age test satisfied the other program's §1302.12(b) requirement — the companion test flips prove it (`-...participant_meets_age_requirements_under_paragraph_b: holds` / `-...#migrant_or_seasonal_participant_eligible: holds` become `+...head_start_migrant_or_seasonal_age_requirement_met: not_holds` for a 2-year-old who fails (b)(3)), and in an ordinary (non-Tribal, non-MSHS) context the bridge returned false for a participant who does meet (b). Separately, §1302.12(c)(1) reads "A pregnant woman or a child is eligible if" (pinned release us-rulespec-2026-07-24, body sha ec9bc785...), yet the pre-fix (c)/(d)/participation outputs were the bare imported family-level predicates, so they held for a person outside the statutory subject class; the fix adds `participant_is_child or participant_is_pregnant_woman` to exactly those outputs. Both corrections are about which program, which population, and which output surface the rule speaks for, so wrong_entity_or_scope fits better than polarity_or_logic (the OR is the mechanism, the scope conflation is the error) or unrepresented_clause (the added clause is a population restriction).

+          )
+          and paragraph_c_participant_eligible
triage.verifier_notes: Three refutation angles I tested, two of which partly land and should temper the record. (1) The added `head_start_runtime_inputs_valid` fail-closed domain contract (`family_income >= 0`, `poverty_line_amount > 0`, shares in [0,1], `child_age_years >= 0`) has no basis in 45 CFR 1302.12 — the provision says nothing about negative income or a zero poverty line. That piece is defensive precision the module never claimed, i.e. not itself a fidelity defect, and it is the part of the reviewer's quote ("numeric runtime leaves fail OPEN with no domain contract") that would be polarity_or_logic if counted. It should not carry the kind; the age-bridge and subject-predicate defects do. (2) The new inputs `head_start_tribal_program` and `head_start_participant_in_approved_tribal_service_area` are NOT a missing-gate fix: the pre-fix import `us:regulations/45-cfr/1302/12#tribal_service_area_participant_eligible` already contained `tribal_program and participant_in_approved_service_area` (verified at parent fc95ef85, us/regulations/45-cfr/1302/12.yaml lines ~174-192). Those inputs are re-localization of the (e)/(f) conditions after the module stopped importing the two reg outputs, not new coverage. (3) The subject-predicate omission does not change the terminal answers: pre-fix `head_start_eligible` already required `participant_is_child` and `early_head_start_eligible` already required pregnant-or-child, so the (c)(1) subject fix corrects the published intermediate outputs (`head_start_paragraph_c_path_satisfied`, `head_start_additional_allowance_path_satisfied`, `head_start_participation_path_satisfied`) rather than eligibility results — an output-surface scope defect, still real, but narrower than "wrong eligibility answer". The dual-context contamination is the one piece that reaches a regulation-level eligibility output. Commit body is empty and the subject ("Fix Head Start eligibility boundaries") is generic; the evidence is the diff plus the PR #1010 issue comment.
